passages.text: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “Do Not Destroy.” A Miktam of David.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this song.
He called it a Miktam.
He gave it to the choirmaster.
He said to sing it to the tune “Do Not Destroy.”

passages.text: Do you indeed speak justly, O rulers? Do you judge uprightly, O sons of men?
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
He gave it to the choirmaster.
He said, “Do not destroy.”
He called it a Miktam.
He spoke to the rulers.
He asked them a question.
He said, “Do you speak justly?”
He asked, “Do you judge uprightly?”
He called them sons of men.
passages.original: לַמְנַצֵּ֥חַ אַל־ תַּשְׁחֵ֗ת לְדָוִ֥ד מִכְתָּֽם׃ הַֽאֻמְנָ֗ם אֵ֣לֶם צֶ֭דֶק תְּדַבֵּר֑וּן מֵישָׁרִ֥ים תִּ֝שְׁפְּט֗וּ בְּנֵ֣י אָדָֽם׃

passages.text: No, in your hearts you devise injustice; with your hands you mete out violence on the earth.
passages.sermon: You do not act justly.\r\nYou plan evil in your hearts.\r\nYou use your hands to bring violence on the earth.
passages.original: אַף־ בְּלֵב֮ עוֹלֹ֪ת תִּפְעָ֫ל֥וּן בָּאָ֡רֶץ חֲמַ֥ס יְ֝דֵיכֶ֗ם תְּפַלֵּֽסֽוּן׃

passages.text: The wicked are estranged from the womb; the liars go astray from birth.
passages.sermon:
The wicked turn away from God from the very beginning of life.
They are separated from what is right even from the womb.
Liars begin to wander from the truth as soon as they are born.
They speak falsehood from their earliest days.
passages.original: זֹ֣רוּ רְשָׁעִ֣ים מֵרָ֑חֶם תָּע֥וּ מִ֝בֶּ֗טֶן דֹּבְרֵ֥י כָזָֽב׃

passages.text: Their venom is like the venom of a snake, like a cobra that shuts its ears, refusing to hear the tune of the charmer who skillfully weaves his spell.
passages.sermon:
The wicked have venom inside them.
Their venom is like the venom of a snake.
Their venom is like the venom of a cobra.
The cobra shuts its ears.
The cobra does not listen to the charmer.
The charmer plays music skillfully.
The cobra refuses to hear the charmer’s tune.
passages.original: חֲמַת־ לָ֗מוֹ כִּדְמ֥וּת חֲמַת־ נָחָ֑שׁ כְּמוֹ־ פֶ֥תֶן חֵ֝רֵ֗שׁ יַאְטֵ֥ם אָזְנֽוֹ׃ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־ יִ֭שְׁמַע לְק֣וֹל מְלַחֲשִׁ֑ים חוֹבֵ֖ר חֲבָרִ֣ים מְחֻכָּֽם׃

passages.text: O God, shatter their teeth in their mouths; O LORD, tear out the fangs of the lions.
passages.sermon:
God, act with power.
Break the teeth of the wicked in their mouths.
Lord, remove the fangs from these fierce enemies.
They are like young lions.
Destroy their strength completely.
passages.original: אֱ‍ֽלֹהִ֗ים הֲרָס־ שִׁנֵּ֥ימוֹ בְּפִ֑ימוֹ מַלְתְּע֥וֹת כְּ֝פִירִ֗ים נְתֹ֣ץ׀ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: May they vanish like water that runs off; when they draw the bow, may their arrows be blunted.
passages.sermon:
The wicked are the subject of this passage.
The wicked act with violence and evil.
May the wicked disappear quickly.
May they vanish like water that flows away.
When the wicked prepare to attack,
May their arrows become dull and useless.
passages.original: יִמָּאֲס֣וּ כְמוֹ־ מַ֭יִם יִתְהַלְּכוּ־ לָ֑מוֹ יִדְרֹ֥ךְ חִצּוֹ כְּמ֣וֹ יִתְמֹלָֽלוּ׃

passages.text: Like a slug that dissolves in its slime, like a woman’s stillborn child, may they never see the sun.
passages.sermon:
The psalmist prays against the wicked.
He asks God to judge them.
He says, “Let them be like a slug that melts away as it moves.”
He says, “Let them be like a stillborn child who never sees the sun.”
passages.original: כְּמ֣וֹ שַׁ֭בְּלוּל תֶּ֣מֶס יַהֲלֹ֑ךְ נֵ֥פֶל אֵ֝֗שֶׁת בַּל־ חָ֥זוּ שָֽׁמֶשׁ׃

passages.text: Before your pots can feel the burning thorns— whether green or dry— He will sweep them away.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
Saul sent men to watch David’s house and to kill him.
David speaks to his enemies.
God acts quickly against the wicked.
Before your cooking pots feel the heat from burning thorns, God will act.
God will sweep the wicked away.
He will do this whether the thorns are green or dry.
passages.original: בְּטֶ֤רֶם יָבִ֣ינוּ סִּֽירֹתֵיכֶ֣ם אָטָ֑ד כְּמוֹ־ חַ֥י כְּמוֹ־ חָ֝ר֗וֹן יִשְׂעָרֶֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: The righteous will rejoice when they see they are avenged; they will wash their feet in the blood of the wicked.
passages.sermon:
The righteous person sees God bring justice.
The righteous person feels joy when God avenges them.
The righteous person stands over the wicked.
The righteous person washes their feet in the blood of the wicked.
passages.original: יִשְׂמַ֣ח צַ֭דִּיק כִּי־ חָזָ֣ה נָקָ֑ם פְּעָמָ֥יו יִ֝רְחַ֗ץ בְּדַ֣ם הָרָשָֽׁע׃

passages.text: Then men will say, “There is surely a reward for the righteous! There is surely a God who judges the earth!”
passages.sermon:
People will speak.
They will say, “The righteous receive a reward.”
They will say, “God exists.”
God judges on the earth.
passages.original: וְיֹאמַ֣ר אָ֭דָם אַךְ־ פְּרִ֣י לַצַּדִּ֑יק אַ֥ךְ יֵשׁ־ אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים שֹׁפְטִ֥ים בָּאָֽרֶץ׃
